p:cNvPr.descr: This diagram illustrates the epinephrine cascade. Epinephrine triggers a series of reactions in hepatocytes in which catalysts activate catalysts, resulting in great amplification of the original hormone signal. This diagram illustrates the epinephrine cascade. In this diagram, one molecule of epinephrine, represented as a small wrinkled purple pea shape, is fed into an epinephrine-receptor complex, represented by a tannish pink structure attached to a green, snail like shape – this is the hepatocyte. There’s a dashed arrow pointing from the hepatocyte to a green oval structure with hair-like projections all around it, labeled Gs alpha. A purple rectangle is to the right and has the text, 10 molecules, written in it. There’s a diagonal dashed arrow pointing from the Gs alpha left and downward to a small green outlined circle with a solid green triangle in it; this shape sits on top of a black arrow pointing to the right and represents adenylyl cyclase, written in blue. To the left of this arrow is ATP, and to the right is Cyclic AMP. Next to this on the right is another purple rectangle with 200 molecules written in it. Cyclic AMP is fed into the next reaction, as indicated by a curved arrow feeding into an arrow pointing right. To the left of this is inactive PKA, and to the right od the arrow is Active PKA. Next to this is a purple rectangle with 100 molecules written in it. A dashed diagonal arrow points left and downward to the green structure representing adenylyl cyclase, sitting on top of an arrow pointing right. To the left of this arrow is inactive phosphorylase b kinase, and to the rigt of the arrow is active phosphorylase b kinase. To the right is a purple rectangle with 1,000 molecules in it.A dashed diagonal arrow points left and downward to the green structure representing adenylyl cyclase, sitting on top of an arrow pointing right. To the left of the arrow is inactive glycogen phosphorylase b, and to the right of the arrow is active glycogen phosphorylase a. To the right is a purple rectangle with 10,000 molecules written in it. A dashed diagonal arrow points left and downward to the green structure representing adenylyl cyclase, sitting on top of an arrow pointing right. To the left of the arrow is glycogen, and to the right is Glucose-1-phosphate. Below the Glucose-1-phosphase is a purple rectangle that has 100,000 molecules written in it. Below this, there is an arrow pointing downward to glucose; then, another arrow points down to blood glucose. Below it is another purple rectangle that has 100,000 molecules written in it.
